question: Should OpenClaw accept a new public operator-admin Gateway RPC, `agents.setDefault`, for changing the default agent, or should clients continue using the existing config write APIs?
rationale: Source inspection proves the method is missing, but adding a Gateway/protocol/SDK/Admin HTTP write method creates a public API contract and new operator action that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the RPC
options.body: Use the linked PR as the canonical implementation path, with compatibility review for the additive Gateway, protocol, SDK, and Admin HTTP surfaces.

options.title: Keep config writes only
options.body: Reject the new RPC surface and ask desktop/web clients to continue using `config.set` or `config.patch` for default-agent changes.

options.title: Defer to broader agent API design
options.body: Keep the product need open only if maintainers want to redesign agent-management mutations together rather than adding this one method.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the RPC
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR as the canonical implementation path, with compatibility review for the additive Gateway, protocol, SDK, and Admin HTTP surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and prepared the original Gateway agent CRUD method family, so they are a practical routing owner for whether this method belongs with that family.
